title: A form of refined Roth's theorem and its application to the $abc$-conjecture

snippets.content: We begin by recalling some notations and notions. Let κ be a number field and κ̄ an algebraic closure of κ. Let O_κ denote the ring of integers of κ. Let M_κ be the canonical set of distinct inequivalent valuations of κ satisfying the product formula. Here ||·||_v is normalized by its absolute value. A non-Archimedean place v ∈ M_κ corresponds to a nonzero prime ideal p = p_v ⊆ O_κ. If v is Archimedean, then v corresponds to a real embedding σ : κ → ℝ or a complex conjugate pair of complex embeddings. Let M_κ⁰ be the set of non-Archimedean places and M_κ^∞ be the set of all Archimedean places. Let S be a finite subset of M_κ containing all Archimedean valuations. Defines proximity function m(x,a) and valence function N(x,a). The relative multiplicative heights H_κ(x), H_{*,κ}(x) and absolute logarithmic height h(x) are defined.
\prod_{v \in M_\kappa} \|x\|_v = \prod_{v \in M_\kappa} |x|_v^{n_v} = 1, \ x \in \kappa^* = \kappa - \{0\}.
\|x\|_v = |x|_v^{n_v} = \mathcal{N}(\mathfrak{p})^{-v_\mathfrak{p}(x)}
\chi_v(x, a) = \begin{cases} \frac{|x - a|_v}{|x|_v \vee |a|_v} & : x, a \in \kappa \\ \frac{1}{|x|_v} & : a = \infty \end{cases}
\chi_v(x, a) = \begin{cases} \frac{|x - a|_v}{(1 + |x|_v^2)^{1/2}(1 + |a|_v^2)^{1/2}} & : x, a \in \kappa \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + |x|_v^2}} & : a = \infty \end{cases}
m(x, a) = \frac{1}{[\kappa : \mathbb{Q}]} \sum_{v \in S} \log \frac{1}{\chi_v(x, a)^{n_v}}
N(x, a) = \frac{1}{[\kappa : \mathbb{Q}]} \sum_{v \in M_\kappa - S} \log \frac{1}{\chi_v(x, a)^{n_v}}
\max \{ 1, \frac{1}{|x - a|_v} \} \leq \frac{1}{\chi_v(x, a)} \leq C \max \{ 1, \frac{1}{|x - a|_v} \}
H_\kappa(x) = (\prod_{v \in M_\kappa^\infty} (\sqrt{1 + |x|_v^2})^{n_v}) (\prod_{v \in M_\kappa - M_\kappa^\infty} \max\{1, |x|_v^{n_v}\})
h(x) = \frac{1}{[\kappa : \mathbb{Q}]} \log H_\kappa(x)

Theorem 1.1. Let κ be a number field and S ⊂ M_κ a finite subset of absolute values on κ. Assume that each absolute value in S has been extended in some way to κ̄. Let a₁, ..., a_q be distinct elements in κ̄ and ε a positive constant. Then there are only finitely many x ∈ κ such that ∏_{v∈S} (min{1, 1/||x||_v} ∏_{j=1}^q min{1, ||x - a_j||_v}) < 1/H_{*,κ}(x)^{2+ε}.
\prod_{v \in S} \min\{1, \frac{1}{\|x\|_v}\} \prod_{j=1}^q \min\{1, \|x - a_j\|_v\} < \frac{1}{H_{*,κ}(x)^{2+\epsilon}}
(q - 1) h(x) \leq N(x, \infty) + \sum_{j=1}^q N(x, a_j) + \epsilon h(x) + O(1)
N(x, a_j) = \frac{1}{[\kappa : \mathbb{Q}]} \sum_{v \in S^c(x-a_j)} \operatorname{ord}_v(x - a_j) \log N(\mathfrak{p}_v) + O(1)
\overline{N}(x, a_j) = \frac{1}{[\kappa : \mathbb{Q}]} \sum_{v \in S^c(x-a_j)} \log N(\mathfrak{p}_v)
Conjecture 1.2. Let a₁, ..., a_q be distinct elements in κ̄ and ε a positive constant. All but finitely many x ∈ κ satisfy the inequality (q-1)h(x) ≤ N̄(x,∞) + ∑_{j=1}^q N̄(x,a_j) + εh(x) + O(1).

Conjecture 1.3 (abc-conjecture). Given ε > 0, there exists C(ε) such that for any nonzero relatively prime integers a, b, c with a + b = c: max{|a|,|b|,|c|} ≤ C(ε) r(abc)^{1+ε}, where r(abc) = ∏_{p|abc} p is the radical of abc.
Theorem 1.4. Let a₁, ..., a_q be distinct elements in κ̄. All but finitely many algebraic integers x ∈ κ satisfy the inequality (q-1)h(x) ≤ ∑_{j=1}^q N(x, a_j) + O(1).

Theorem 1.5. Let a₁, a₂ be distinct elements in κ̄. All but finitely many simple numbers x ∈ κ satisfy the inequality h(x) ≤ N(x,∞) + N(x,a₁) + N(x,a₂) + O(1). A number x ∈ κ is called simple if negative powers of ideals occurred in x are all −1.

Theorem 1.6. For any nonzero relatively prime integers a, b, c such that a + b = c and that one of a, b, c only has prime factors of power 1, we have max{|a|,|b|,|c|} ≤ C r(abc), where C is an absolute constant.

Some results that would follow from the abc-conjecture can be found in [1], [8], pp. 185-188, [14]; see also [2], [5], [6], [15]. In [10], C. L. Stewart and R. Tijdeman proved that max{|a|,|b|,|c|} < exp{C r(abc)^{15}}. In [11], Stewart and Yu obtained max{|a|,|b|,|c|} < exp{C(ε) r(abc)^{2/3+ε}}. In [12], Stewart and Yu further proved max{|a|,|b|,|c|} < exp{C(ε) r(abc)^{1/3+ε}}.
We consider the rational function Q(X) = 1/((X-a₁)...(X-a_q)) = ∑ A_j/(X-a_j), where A_j = 1/∏_{i≠j}(a_j-a_i). Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 1.5 will follow from Theorem 2.1.

Theorem 2.1. Let a₁, ..., a_q be distinct elements in κ and ε a positive constant. There exist an extension field K of κ and an element x' ∈ K such that all but finitely many x ∈ κ satisfy (q-1)h(x) ≤ N̄(x,∞) + ∑_{j=1}^q N̄(x,a_j) + 2m(x'Q(x),∞) + O(1).

Proof of Theorem 2.1. Sets ρ_v = min|A_j|_v, σ_v = max|A_j|_v, δ_v = min|a_i-a_j|_v, E_{vj} = {x : |x-a_j|_v < δ_v/(2ϰ_v)} with ϰ_v = 1/2 + (q-1)σ_v/ρ_v. Shows |x-a_i|_v ≥ δ_v/(2ϰ_v) for i≠j, x∈E_{vj}. Derives |Q(x)|_v > ρ_v/(2|x-a_j|_v) and log⁺||Q(x)||_v > log⁺(1/||x-a_j||_v) - n_v log(2/ρ_v) ≥ ∑_{i=1}^q log⁺(1/||x-a_i||_v) - q n_v log⁺(2ϰ_v/δ_v) - n_v log(2/ρ_v). This yields m(Q(x),∞) ≥ ∑ m(x,a_j) - C_S. Computes m(Q(x),∞) in terms of x'Q(x) using field extension K. Derives inequality (15): m(x,∞)+∑m(x,a_j) ≤ 2h(x) - N_{x'}(x) + S_{j,x'}(x) + O(1) and (16): (q-1)h(x) ≤ N(x,∞)+∑N(x,a_j) - N_{x'}(x) + S_{x'}(x) + O(1). Claims existence of constant c_v such that c_v∏|x'/(x-a_j)|_{v+} ≤ |x'/((x-a₁)...(x-a_q))|_{v+}^q (estimate 17). Provides case analysis based on |x-a_i|_v relative to δ_v/2 and |x'|_v relative to δ_v/2. Concludes S_{x'}(x) ≤ 2m(x'Q(x),∞) + O(1) (estimate 18) and the desired inequality (19). Constructs x' using extension field K via principal ideal result from [3, Theorem 2.32]. Completes proof.
\varkappa_v = \frac{1}{2} + (q-1)\frac{\sigma_v}{\rho_v}

Remark. x' can be constructed so that it belongs to κ (but hard to compute m(x'Q(x),∞)). Provides explicit construction via ideal factorization: (x) = P₁^{t₁}...P_l^{t_l} h^{-1}, (x-a_j) factorizations with prime ideals p_i and q_j from M_κ-S and S respectively. Constructs a₀ = ∏ p_i^{r_i-1} and ideals d_i via p_i^{r_i} d_i = a₀ p₁...p_{m_q}. Uses sum-of-elements δ₁+...+δ_{m_q}=1 with δ_i∈d_i. Determines α_i with p_i^{r_i-1}|α_i, p_i^{r_i}∤α_i. Constructs x₀ = ∑α_iδ_i with property a₀|x₀. Handles non-distinct case with replacement. Similarly constructs x_∞ for denominator. Takes x' = x₀/x_∞ ∈ κ*.

Proof of Theorem 1.4. Arguments are true over K. If x is an algebraic integer, then y = 1/(x'Q(x)) is an algebraic integer, so m(x'Q(x),∞) = m(y,0) = h(y) - N(y,0) + O(1) = m(y,∞) - N(y,0) + O(1). By Dirichlet's unit theorem, ∃c(κ) with |y|_v ≤ c(κ)|y|_w for any Archimedean v,w. Choose v with 1 ≤ |y|_v = max_w |y|_w. Then m(y,0) = ∑_{w∈S} log⁺(1/||y||_w) + O(1) = O(1). Thus (q-1)h(x) ≤ N(x,∞) + ∑_{j=1}^q N(x,a_j) + O(1).
Proof of Theorem 1.5. Since x is simple, y = 1/(x'Q(x)) is an algebraic integer, where q = 2. The proof can be completed in the same way as for Theorem 1.4.

Proof of Theorem 1.6. Apply (12) to x = a/c. Since one of a,b,c only has prime factors of power 1. Taking abc-point y with reduced representation (a,b,c) and applying (12) to x=a/c yields h(a/c) ≤ N̄(a/c,0) + N̄(a/c,-1) + N̄(a/c,∞) + O(1). Since a+b+c=0 and a,b,c are relatively prime: N̄(a/c,0) = (1/[κ:ℚ])∑_{v∈S^c(a)} log N(p_v), N̄(a/c,-1) = (1/[κ:ℚ])∑_{v∈S^c(b)} log N(p_v), N̄(a/c,∞) = (1/[κ:ℚ])∑_{v∈S^c(c)} log N(p_v). Thus h(a/c) ≤ N̄(y,E) + O(1) and similarly h(b/c) ≤ N̄(y,E) + O(1). Since h(y) = max{h(a/c),h(b/c)} + O(1), combining yields h(y) ≤ N̄(y,E) + O(1), and (13) follows.
\max \{ |a|, |b|, |c| \} \leq C(\epsilon) r(abc)^{1+\epsilon}
(q-1) h(x) \leq \sum_{j=1}^{q} N(x, a_j) + O(1)
h(x) \leq N(x, \infty) + N(x, a_1) + N(x, a_2) + O(1)
